Jackson County by the numbers

Who sends and who collects the property tax bill in Jackson County, MO?

Two county departments split the work. The Assessment Department values every parcel, and the Department of Collection mails the bills and takes payment. If your question is about what the house is worth on paper, call Assessment at 816-881-1330. If it is about what you owe or how to pay, call Collection at 816-881-3232.

Assessment keeps real property customer service at 1300 Washington St. in Kansas City, and individual personal property at the Historic Truman Courthouse, 112 W. Lexington in Independence. Both counters open at 8 a.m. and close at 5 p.m. on weekdays, and holidays the county observes are closed. Collection also works from both courthouses and answers email at Collections@jacksongov.org.

A seller in Jackson County, Missouri should pull the parcel record from the county's public property access portal before listing. It shows the assessed figures that the bill is built from.

What does Jackson County cover, and who lives here?

Jackson County sits on the Kansas border in western Missouri and has two county seats, Independence and Kansas City. It was organized on December 15, 1826, and the Missouri River forms most of its northern edge. Neighbors include Clay, Cass and Lafayette counties in Missouri and Johnson and Wyandotte counties in Kansas.

The county counts 19 communities, among them Blue Springs, Grandview, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Oak Grove, Grain Valley and Sugar Creek. All of them share one assessment and collection system, with each taxing district adding its own levy line to the statement.

  • Land area: 604.52 square miles
  • Residents counted in the 2025 Census estimate: 732,994, up 2.2% from the 2020 base
  • Homes and apartments: 344,038 units
  • Share of households that own: 59.1%
  • Middle price tag on an owned home: $230,500

Median household income across the 2020 to 2024 survey years is $68,577, and typical gross rent is $1,197. Those who carry a mortgage report a median of $1,639 a month in owner costs, taxes included.

When is the Jackson County property tax bill due?

The bill is due on December 31. The county mails bills during November, and for 2025 the mailing was expected to finish by December 12. If nothing has arrived by about December 8, call the Collector, because an unreceived bill still carries the same deadline.

A mailed check counts only if the USPS stamps it by year end, and the county suggests mailing several days ahead because drop-box mail does not always get a same-day postmark. Checks go to the Jackson County Collector with the property account number written on them. Online payment through payments.jacksongov.org stops at 11:40 p.m. on December 31, and the two courthouse drop boxes lock at midnight that night. Cash should never go in a drop box.

Fees for paying online are a $2.00 transaction charge, plus $1.25 for an e-check or 2.75% for a debit or credit card. Paying in person or by check avoids those add-ons.

What are the key dates and steps for a Jackson County tax year?

What is the process to contest a Jackson County assessment?

Start with the Board of Equalization, an independent panel of county taxpayers that now sits only at 1300 Washington in Kansas City. The 2026 application window ran until July 13, 2026, so that deadline has passed. Watch the board's page for the 2027 window.

Evidence that carries weight includes a certified appraiser's report, a sales contract with the settlement statement for a recent purchase, and written repair estimates. The board will not look at evidence shown on a phone or tablet at the hearing, and it does not make copies for you.

  • If you signed a stipulated value offered by Assessment, your board appeal is cancelled and you can no longer go to the State Tax Commission.
  • If you skip the stipulation, you keep the hearing, and a loss there can be taken to the State Tax Commission.
  • Commercial appeals to the Commission require a lawyer.
  • Withdrawing an appeal must be in writing from the homeowner and can be done any time.

Must the full bill be paid while a Jackson County appeal is open?

Yes. The county tells owners to pay the printed amount before year end, even when a hearing is still ahead. Recalculations for 2026 appeal decisions are suspended until January 2027, and when a lower value is set, the excess is refunded automatically.

Paying under protest is optional. Missouri statute 139.031 asks for full payment before the delinquency date plus a written statement of the grounds and the value you claim. The county notes that a protest can slow a refund, since protested money is released only on a set schedule, and that protesting does not protect or harm your right to appeal. Partial payments are taken for real property, but interest, penalties and fees accrue on whatever remains unpaid after December 31, and partial payments cannot be made online.

Is there a cap or credit on residential assessments in Jackson County?

The county announced a 15% assessment cap for qualifying residential homeowners, tied to a review of the 2023 single-family assessments. Per the county's FAQ sheet updated December 8, 2025, relief comes as a credit on the 2026, 2027 and 2028 bills, spread evenly across those three years. No application is needed, no refund checks go out, and the 2025 bill still had to be paid in full.

The county says the tax money had already been distributed to schools, fire districts, libraries and cities, which is why it is a credit and not a check. The relief covers residential real estate only, and vehicles and boats are not part of it. Call Assessment if your bill looks wrong rather than assuming a credit has posted.

Which senior programs exist for Jackson County homeowners?

Two county programs apply to residential property, and an eligible owner may use both. The Senior Property Tax Credit offsets future increases. The Senior Citizen Quad Payment Program lets the owner spread the county bill over four equal installments with no interest or penalties.

  • Both require age 62 or older by December 31 of the relevant year and the home as the only primary residence.
  • The Quad program also requires prior-year taxes to be current, a home assessed solely as residential, and ownership by the person, not a trust.
  • Taxes paid from a mortgage escrow are not eligible for the Quad program.
  • The credit covers ad valorem principal only. Special assessments and CID or TDD charges are due in full.

The state Circuit Breaker credit is a separate program run by the Missouri Department of Revenue at 573-751-3505.

Who owes the tax after a Jackson County house changes hands?

Unpaid real estate tax attaches to the parcel itself, so the incoming owner answers for any balance. The county explains that the year's tax is usually split between the two parties, with the buyer credited for the days the seller held title. Normally no money goes to the Collector at the sale itself, though a closing company may pay any amount that is currently due.

Tell the Assessment office the new owner and mailing address, because a bill can otherwise go to the seller's old address. When a lender pays from escrow, send the bill on to the lender. Ask the closing company which tax year it is prorating.

More questions about Jackson County, MO Property Tax Guide

When does Jackson County, MO stop accepting on-time property tax payments?

At the end of December 31. A mailed check must be postmarked by then, and the online system cuts off at 11:40 p.m. Interest, penalties and fees start accruing the next day.

Is it too late to contest my 2026 Jackson County value?

Yes. The 2026 filing window at the Board of Equalization ended July 13, 2026. Look for the 2027 window on the board's page, and pay the 2026 bill in full by December 31 meanwhile.

Does a refund after a value cut require a protest payment?

No. A lower value triggers an automatic refund, and a protest can slow it down. A protest payment must be on time, in full and accompanied by a written statement.

How is the tax split when a Jackson County home sells midyear?

The buyer owes the full bill by December 31, while the seller's share usually appears as a credit to the buyer at closing. Ask the closing company how your contract divides it.

What address do I use to mail a Jackson County tax payment?

Make it payable to the Jackson County Collector with the property account number on it. Protest payments go to Attention: Protest, P.O. Box 219747, Kansas City, MO 64121-9747. Call 816-881-3232 for the current regular mailing address.

Greene County by the numbers

Which Greene County offices deal with property tax?

Three county offices touch a Springfield-area tax bill. The Assessor values the property, the County Clerk runs the appeals board and builds the tax book, and the Collector of Revenue bills and takes payment. The Collector's page says the Assessor's values go to the Clerk, who applies the levies voters approved to produce the yearly tax book.

  • Collector of Revenue Allen Icet: (417) 868-4036, open weekdays from 8:00 with no lunch closure, and shut on November 26 and 27, 2026
  • Assessor Brent Johnson: 940 N Boonville Ave, Room 35, Springfield, (417) 868-4101 for real estate and (417) 868-4195 for personal property
  • County Clerk and Board of Equalization: 940 North Boonville, Springfield, MO 65802

The Assessor's door opens at 8:00 on most weekdays and at 8:30 on Wednesday, and both offices close at 4:30. The Collector's site lets owners look up statements and receipts, and card payments carry a processor charge of 1.5 percent for debit and 2.3 percent for credit (with a $2 minimum), or $1 for an e-check. That charge goes to the processor and not to the county.

After an online payment, the receipt posts to your account on the site within about three hours and is not emailed. Pay in the office when you need a receipt the same day, for example at a closing.

What does Greene County look like to someone selling a house?

Greene County lies in southwest Missouri, in the Ozark foothills, with Springfield as its seat and biggest city. The county was organized in 1833 and carries the name of Revolutionary War general Nathanael Greene. Wilson's Creek National Battlefield sits inside it. It borders Polk, Dallas, Webster, Christian, Lawrence and Dade counties.

Besides Springfield, the cities and towns are Ash Grove, Battlefield, Fair Grove, Republic, Rogersville, Strafford, Walnut Grove and Willard. Roughly 86 percent of residents were counted in urban areas in 2020.

From the Census QuickFacts table for Greene County:

  • 309,286 residents in the July 2025 estimate, and 442.6 people per square mile of land in 2020
  • 142,405 housing units, with 57.5 percent of homes owner-occupied
  • $221,300 median value of owner-occupied homes (2020 to 2024) beside a $989 median gross rent
  • $61,479 median household income
  • 966 building permits in 2025

How does the Greene County Assessor reach a value?

The Assessor is elected for four years, and Brent Johnson has held the office since 2021. The office's job is to list every taxable parcel and assess it each year as of January 1. It also maintains the tax map, changing parcel lines when the Recorder of Deeds sends warranty deeds, so a lot split or combined shows up there after the deed is recorded.

The state formula in RSMo 137.115 sets the residential ratio at 19 percent, with fresh values arriving in odd-numbered years such as 2027. A house increase above 15 percent has to be backed by an on-site inspection.

The Assessor runs a Public Access website, updated nightly, that shows address, owner, taxing district, school district, section, township and range, and map layers for lots, fire districts and city limits. Use it to confirm the taxing districts before comparing your bill with a neighbor's.

What are the steps to appeal a Greene County assessment?

Greene County's Clerk lays out three steps, shown in the table. The informal step is optional, and the County Clerk's page confirms that skipping it does not stop an owner from filing a formal appeal.

Greene County real estate appeal path, per the County Clerk
StepWhereDeadline
Informal talk with an appraiserAssessor, (417) 868-4101As soon as the notice arrives
Formal appealCounty Clerk, 940 North BoonvilleSecond Monday in July (July 13 in 2026)
State appealMissouri State Tax CommissionSeptember 30, or a month after the Board rules if that is later

The 2026 form deadline has passed. For the 2027 reassessment the same rule points to the second Monday in July, which is July 12, 2027.

The Board of Equalization has eight members, three named by the County Commission and five by the City of Springfield, and it meets at 9:00 a.m. on the second Tuesday of each month at 1126 N Boonville to certify tax book corrections. Each July it hears formal appeals, and in 2026 those hearings were in Room 212 of the Historic Greene County Courthouse. At the hearing the Assessor presents evidence for the value, and the owner answers with evidence of their own. The Board may raise, lower or leave the figure alone.

Does Greene County have a senior property tax freeze?

Yes. The Collector runs a Senior Tax Credit that lets qualifying seniors lock their real estate tax bill so it stays frozen in future years. Applications run January 1 through June 30 each year, so the window for 2026 has closed and the next opens January 1, 2027.

Collector Allen Icet announced that annual renewal is no longer required as of January 1, 2026. Credit holders must report a change in ownership or occupancy within 45 days and answer any audit request within 45 days. Remote applications need a copy of a government photo ID that shows the date of birth.

This matters when a house is sold. Report the sale within the 45 days, and ask the Collector's office what happens to the credit when ownership changes.

What happens to Greene County taxes that go unpaid?

A bill still open on January 1 picks up the statutory penalty (RSMo 140.100), set at 18 percent of the year's delinquency. Mailed payments are judged by postmark.

An owner contesting a value can pay in full before the delinquency date and file a written statement with the Collector naming the grounds and the claimed value. RSMo 139.031 then requires a suit against the Collector within 90 days. The State Tax Commission adds that an appeal can be filed before the bill is paid, but penalty and interest still apply if the bill is late.

Land with unpaid years can be offered at the August tax sale after the owner of record has been notified by mail. The owner can still pay off the balance before the sale. Ask the Collector at (417) 868-4036 for current figures.

How should I deal with property tax when selling a Greene County house?

Look up the parcel on the Collector's statements and receipts page, print what is owed and give the figure to the title company. Check the Public Access map for the school and fire district, since buyers ask. If a senior credit is on the property, tell the Collector about the sale within the 45 day window.

Owners holding a vacant inherited home, a long tenant lease or a roof that needs work can ask for a written cash offer, with the tax balance settled out of the price at closing.

More questions about Greene County, MO Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Greene County property tax?

To the Greene County Collector of Revenue, online or in person, at (417) 868-4036. Weekday hours run until 4:30 p.m. Card and e-check payments carry a processor fee, and online receipts post within about three hours.

What was the 2026 Greene County appeal deadline?

July 13, 2026, the second Monday in July. The County Clerk had to receive the Board of Equalization form by then. That date has passed, and the 2027 deadline falls on the second Monday in July.

Do I have to see the Assessor before filing an appeal?

No. The County Clerk says an informal meeting with the Assessor is not required before a Board of Equalization appeal. Many owners still call the Assessor at (417) 868-4101 first because concerns are often settled there.

Can a Greene County senior freeze property tax?

Yes, through the Collector's Senior Tax Credit. Applications are taken January 1 to June 30. Annual renewal stopped being required on January 1, 2026, but ownership or occupancy changes must be reported within 45 days.

Who sits on the Greene County Board of Equalization?

Eight taxpayer citizens. The County Commission appoints three and the City of Springfield appoints five. The County Clerk serves as non-voting secretary, and the Board hears formal appeals each July.

Which Jasper County, MO offices handle my property tax?

The Assessor sets the value and the Collector sends the bill and takes the money. Jasper County has Lisa Perry as Assessor and Steven E. McIntosh as Collector. Both have a presence at the Carthage courthouse, 302 S. Main, and the Collector also staffs the Joplin Courts Building at 633 S. Pearl.

  • Assessor, personal property: 417-358-0437

Counter hours at the Collector's offices are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The Assessor's office follows state holidays and keeps the same weekday hours.

What kind of county is Jasper County?

Jasper County lies in the southwest corner of Missouri along the Kansas line. Carthage is the county seat, and Joplin, the largest city, is partly in Newton County. The county was organized in 1841 and has 638.51 square miles of land. Webb City, Carl Junction, Oronogo, Sarcoxie and Purcell are among its other cities, and its neighbors are Barton, Dade, Lawrence and Newton counties in Missouri plus Cherokee and Crawford counties in Kansas.

Interstate 44, Interstate 49 and the old Route 66 alignment cross the county, and the Joplin area is also a metropolitan statistical area. In May 2011 an EF5 tornado struck Joplin. For a seller, the practical point is that city, school and fire district levies differ across these towns, and one county bill carries all of them.

The Census Bureau's quick facts for the period 2020 to 2024 give a picture of the housing stock:

  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 127,428
  • Housing units: 56,504
  • Owner-occupied share: 62.8%
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $166,900
  • Median household income: $60,694

Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,219, and without one $491. Median gross rent is $973.

When are Jasper County property taxes due?

Statements are mailed in the first week of November, are due on receipt and turn delinquent after December 31. A mailed payment needs a USPS postmark on or before 12/31/26. The online payment page closes at 11:59 p.m. on 12/31/26, and money sent after that accrues interest and penalties once the site reopens in 2027. A payment postmarked late is returned unprocessed unless the late fees are included.

If no statement shows up by the end of November, the Collector asks you to call right away, and the office reminds owners that a missing statement does not remove the duty to pay. Technical trouble with a phone or online payment does not extend the statutory date, so plan for an in-person visit or the 24-hour drop box at either office if a website acts up.

How do I pay and what does it cost in Jasper County?

Ways to pay a Jasper County, MO tax statement, per the Collector's site

The Collector bills what the Assessor's records show, so errors in a mailing address, legal description or listed vehicle should go to the Assessor, not the Collector. For real estate, call 417-358-0440 and ask about your parcel's value and the notice you received.

Personal property works on a calendar of its own. Assessment lists are mailed in early January, due by March 1 without penalty, and may be filed online with the PIN from the mailed sheet. The Assessor does not accept emailed renditions. Tax is based on what you owned on January 1, even if you sold the vehicle later. Business owners assess equipment and furniture the same way, and landlords with rental or leasing space owe a tenant list by January 30.

A statement of non-assessment, which some call a tax waiver, can be used only to license a vehicle and requires bringing the title or registration to the office in person.

Can I appeal a Jasper County assessment?

Yes, through the county board of equalization. Missouri statute 138.060 directs that board to decide appeals from the assessor's valuation in a summary way, and it says there is no presumption that the assessor's number is right. The statute also puts the burden on the assessor in any other county when a value rose at least fifteen percent from the prior assessment without new construction or improvement.

Ask the Assessor's office, at 417-358-0440, for the filing deadline and hearing procedure for the current year, and bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal or a purchase contract. Pay by December 31 regardless of the appeal outcome, since interest and penalties start after that day.

What relief exists for older Jasper County homeowners?

The SB190 Senior Citizen Tax Credit is handled by the Collector. Applications for the most recent cycle ran from February 2 to May 31, 2026, at Room 107 in the Carthage courthouse, and could be filed online by QR code or PIN from a renewal notice. That window has closed, so ask the Collector when the next one opens.

  • The applicant must be 62 or older by midnight on December 31 of the initial credit year.
  • The home must be in Jasper County and be the applicant's primary residence.
  • The prior year's taxes must have been paid.

Renewal applications were accepted in the same period. The Missouri Department of Revenue runs its own Property Tax Credit for certain seniors and 100% disabled individuals, reachable at 573-751-3505, and that program is separate from the county credit.

What should a seller know about tax at closing in Jasper County?

Call the Collector for a current balance on the parcel before you set a closing date, since statements are due on receipt and become delinquent after December 31. Ask whether the escrow or title agent will pay the current year or prorate it, and put that in the contract. After the sale, the new owner should confirm the mailing address with the Assessor so that the November statement lands in the right mailbox.

Owners who inherited a house in Jasper County and are behind on earlier years should ask the Collector for the amount currently owed on each year before they quote a price to a buyer.

What is the deadline to pay Jasper County property tax?

December 31. Mail needs a USPS postmark on or before 12/31/26, and the online payment page shuts at 11:59 p.m. that night. After that date, interest and penalties apply.

Where do I pay in Jasper County if I live near Joplin?

An e-check carries a $2.00 fee and a credit card costs 2.45% of the balance. The county keeps none of it. A check or an in-person payment has no such charge.

I did not get my statement. Do I still owe?

Yes. The Collector says failing to receive a statement does not cancel the tax, and any penalty and interest still apply. Call if nothing arrives by the end of November.

Call the Jasper County Assessor: 417-358-0440 for real estate or 417-358-0437 for personal property. The Collector bills only what the Assessor's records show.

Jefferson County by the numbers

Which Jefferson County offices send, value and collect the tax?

Three offices share the job. The Assessor values the property, the County Clerk runs the first appeal board, and the Collector sends the bill and takes the payment. All three work from the Administration Center at 729 Maple Street in Hillsboro, the county seat.

  • Assessor, real estate questions: 636-797-5343. Personal property: 636-797-5466. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.
  • County Clerk, Board of Equalization appointments: 636-797-5478.
  • Collector, bills and payments: 636-797-5406, mailing address P.O. Box 100, Hillsboro, MO 63050.

Rates come from the school, fire, ambulance and other districts that cover your parcel, not from the Assessor or Collector. A house in Fox C-6 and a house in Hillsboro R-3 can carry quite different totals for that reason.

What does the Jefferson County housing picture look like for sellers?

Jefferson County sits on the Mississippi River south of St. Louis and covers about 657 square miles of land. Arnold is the largest city, Hillsboro is the seat, and Festus, De Soto, Crystal City, Herculaneum and Pevely fill out the list of incorporated places. The county is part of the St. Louis metropolitan area, and in 1980 it held the mean center of U.S. population (Wikipedia).

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page counts 233,132 residents as of July 2025 and 96,228 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the survey shows a typical owned home worth $237,200, an ownership rate of 82.2% and a median household income of $82,851. Workers spend 30.6 minutes getting to their jobs on average.

With more than four in five households owning, a large share of tax bills here are paid by lenders from escrow, which makes the lender request rule in the due-date section below worth knowing.

How does the Jefferson County Assessor value a home?

The Assessor uses mass appraisal. Replacement cost of the buildings is reduced for depreciation, then land value is added to reach fair market value (Assessor FAQ). Missouri requires every parcel to be reassessed in odd-numbered years, and 2027 is the next one.

Market value is then multiplied by the assessment level for the property class. A $100,000 house is carried at $19,000 of assessed value.

Assessment levels used in Jefferson County (Assessor FAQ)
Property classShare of market value taxed
Residential19%
Commercial32%
Agricultural12%

Your bill can change without a reassessment. A new garage, an adjoining acre or a finished house that had been prorated during construction all move assessed value, and a voter-approved levy change moves the total even when value stays flat.

When is Jefferson County property tax due, and what happens if it is late?

Real estate tax is due December 31 and becomes delinquent on January 1. Bills go on the county website in November and are mailed late that month. If nothing arrives by December 1, call the Collector, because a missing bill does not excuse the deadline.

  • Pay at 729 Maple Street, online, or by the phone line at 1-877-289-0099 (the Collector's FAQ lists a convenience fee of 2.5% with a $1.95 minimum for debit and cards, and $4.95 for e-check).
  • Mailed payments need a postmark of December 31 or earlier, so check the last pickup time at your post office.
  • Mortgage companies must send the Collector a written request for each bill they plan to pay. If you received a paper bill, your lender did not ask for it.

The Collector has no power to waive penalty or interest, citing section 139.100 and an Attorney General opinion. Under RSMo 140.100, land in the back tax book carries an 18 percent penalty on each year's delinquency, and the penalty on land redeemed before sale cannot exceed 2 percent per month.

What are the steps to contest a Jefferson County value?

Start with a phone call to the Assessor. An appraiser reviews the value with you and looks at any evidence you bring. If that does not settle it, you file with the Board of Equalization through the County Clerk. The county's assessor page and the State Tax Commission both give the second Monday in July as the filing cutoff. The 2026 date was July 13 and has passed, and the next one is July 12, 2027.

  1. Call the Assessor at 636-797-5343 and ask for an informal review.
  2. Call the County Clerk at 636-797-5478 for the forms and a hearing date.
  3. Bring five copies of any written evidence: one for each board member, one for the board secretary and one for the Assessor.
  4. Expect a certified letter with the decision, usually within 5 business days.
  5. If you still disagree, file a Complaint for Review of Assessment with the State Tax Commission, attaching the board's decision letter.

The county's collector page gives the State Tax Commission cutoff as September 30 or 30 days after the board decision, whichever is later. The Commission's own guide says the 30 days run from the date of the letter, and that a property owned by an LLC, trust, corporation or estate needs an attorney to file.

Taxes still have to be paid by December 31 while an appeal is open. Paying under protest follows a specific procedure: full payment before the delinquency date plus a written statement of your grounds and your claimed fair market value. Writing "protest" on the check does nothing on its own.

Which tax relief programs apply to Jefferson County homeowners?

The county lists two. One is a Real Property Tax Credit for Seniors, enacted February 15, 2024, with details on the county's Assessor FAQ page. The other is the state's Property Tax Credit Claim, which returns part of the real estate tax or rent paid during the year.

  • The state credit is capped at $1,100 for owners who live in their home and $750 for renters.
  • You may qualify if you are 65 by December 31 of the prior year, or you or your spouse are 100% disabled, or you are 60 or older and receive surviving spouse benefits.
  • Household income, counting Social Security, cannot exceed $30,000 for a single person or $34,000 for married homeowners.
  • File with form MO-1040 and schedule MO-PTS, or form MO-PTC if you do not file an income tax return.

An owner whose house is destroyed by a tornado, flood, fire or earthquake can ask the Assessor to remove the residential value on a pro-rata basis under section 137.082, using the Destroyed Residential Property form.

How are taxes handled when a Jefferson County house sells?

The Collector's FAQ says that in most closings the seller's share of the year's tax is credited on the settlement statement and the buyer is responsible for the full year. Your settlement statement or title company shows the exact split.

Once the new deed is recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office, the Assessor's file shows the new owner. The name on a real estate bill changes only through a recorded deed, so the bill address and the owner name will not update from a phone call alone.

If a house you are selling has a delinquent year, ask the Collector for the amount due including penalty and interest before you accept an offer, and have the title company pay it from the proceeds.

More questions about Jefferson County, MO Property Tax Guide

By what date must a Jefferson County real estate bill be paid?

December 31 of the tax year. Payments postmarked after that date are charged penalty and interest, and the Collector cannot waive either one.

Can I still appeal my 2026 Jefferson County value?

No for the county board. The second Monday in July was July 13, 2026, and has passed. Missouri reassesses in odd-numbered years, so 2027 brings new notices and a July 12, 2027 filing date.

Who do I call if my Jefferson County tax bill never arrived?

Call the Collector at 636-797-5406. The county asks owners to call if nothing has arrived by December 1, and the deadline stays December 31 either way.

Does my mortgage lender pay the Jefferson County bill?

Only if it sent the Collector a written request for your bill. If the paper bill came to you, the lender did not request it, so call the lender to learn where it wants the bill sent.

Who pays the year's tax when I sell my Jefferson County house?

By the Collector's account, the seller's portion is usually credited at closing and the buyer owes the whole year's bill. Your settlement statement lays out the split.

  • 108,090 people in the July 2025 estimate, 3.3 percent more than the 2020 base
  • 48,091 housing units, and 76.5 percent of occupied homes lived in by owners
  • $227,600 typical value for a home lived in by its owner (2020 to 2024 median)
  • $73,165 median household income and a mean commute of 28.3 minutes
  • 794 building permits in 2025

How big is the Franklin County assessment roll?

The Franklin County assessor tracks more than 73,000 parcels with over $1.511 billion in assessed value, the thirteenth highest among Missouri's 114 counties and St. Louis City. Roughly 50,000 parcels are classed residential, 24,000 agricultural and 3,400 commercial. The office says it reassesses all real estate every two years and mails more than 20,000 value-increase notices a year.

Statute fixes the percentages. The residential ratio in RSMo 137.115 is 19 percent of true value, and farm and commercial parcels use their own percentages. Raising a house more than 15 percent without new building requires an on-site inspection first.

The assessor also fields requests from title companies and mortgage lenders, and the county's property search site lets an owner pull up the parcel record before calling. Check the acreage, square footage and bedroom count on the record, since errors there change the value.

What are the key dates on the Franklin County property tax calendar?

The county assessor publishes a yearly calendar that a seller can use to see where a house stands in the cycle. The table lists those dates as the county gives them.

Franklin County assessment and billing calendar, per the assessor
DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for all real and personal property
March 1Personal property list due, with penalties if late
June 30Real estate and personal property rolls go to the County Clerk
Second Monday in JulyLast day to file a Board of Equalization appeal
September 30State Tax Commission deadline, or later if the Board's letter came within the last month
October 1Tax rates set and certified to the County Clerk
November and DecemberCollector prepares and sends bills
December 31Current taxes must be paid before they become delinquent

Source: Franklin County Assessor page. Utilities and railroads report to the assessor by April 1, and the clerk certifies those values by April 20.

How do I challenge a Franklin County valuation?

Begin with the assessor's staff. They hold many informal hearings, mostly in reassessment years, and the office says it tries to settle concerns before they turn into Board filings. Ask which sales the value leans on, then line them up against houses on your own street.

The formal step is the Board of Equalization, with the July deadline shown in the calendar above. Franklin County's assessor page says its own staff presents the facts to the Board. A value that jumped 15 percent or more for reasons other than new building puts the burden on the assessor under RSMo 138.060.

After the Board, the State Tax Commission is the next level, and the county's attorney represents the assessor in that case. A claim that a property should be exempt altogether goes to circuit court instead. Owners that are LLCs, trusts, estates or corporations need a lawyer to file.

Can seniors or disabled owners in Franklin County get property tax relief?

Missouri does not exempt the property of seniors or disabled owners, according to the Franklin County assessor. It points instead to the Missouri Property Tax Credit, which gives income-limited seniors and disabled residents a refund or income tax credit based on property tax or rent paid. Details are at the state Department of Revenue site, and Aging Ahead answers questions at 636-629-3143.

The assessor adds that the Homestead Preservation Act credit needs a legislative appropriation and is not funded at this time.

What happens if Franklin County taxes go unpaid past December 31?

Per the assessor's calendar, a bill left open after December 31 becomes delinquent and draws penalties. The statutory penalty is 18 percent of that year's delinquency (RSMo 140.100), and postmarks decide whether a mailed check was on time.

Owners who dispute a value can still pay in full and file a protest statement with the collector, then sue the collector inside 90 days, as RSMo 139.031 requires. That same section allows a credit or refund for tax paid by mistake when the application comes within three years.

Land with old unpaid years goes into the county's annual August tax sale. Owners can redeem at any point before it by paying the tax, penalty and costs. The Collector can give the figure for a specific parcel at 636-583-6353.

How do I handle property tax when I sell a Franklin County house?

Pull the parcel from the pay site and print the current bill, then ask the Collector at 636-583-6353 whether any earlier year is open. The title company will need the parcel ID and the figure, and who owes which part of the current year is decided by the sales contract.

If the house is inherited, behind on taxes or has tenants or repairs outstanding, a cash purchase can pay the tax balance at the closing table, out of the price. Franklin County deeds are filed at the Recorder of Deeds, and the county website has a Record My Deeds link on its home page.

Where do I pay Franklin County property tax?

At the Collector's office, Room 103, 400 E Locust in Union, or online, by phone at 877-690-3729 with code 3570, or by mail. The county says a nominal convenience fee applies to these services.

When is the Franklin County tax deadline?

December 31. The assessor's calendar says current taxes must be paid by that date, and after it they are delinquent and penalties are applied.

What is the route for contesting a Franklin County assessment?

Call the assessor, then file with the Board of Equalization by its July deadline. If the Board does not change the value, the State Tax Commission is the next stop.

How often does Franklin County reassess homes?

Every two years, according to the assessor's page. New construction gets assessed every year, and the county mails more than 20,000 notices of increased value annually.

Is there property tax relief for Franklin County seniors?

There is a state refund and credit. The Missouri Property Tax Credit helps seniors and disabled residents with limited income. The county assessor notes the Homestead Preservation Act credit is not funded now.

Howell County by the numbers

Who runs property tax in Howell County, and where do I find them?

Both offices work out of the county building on the West Plains square, 35 Court Square. The collector's site names Janet Crow as County Collector and puts the office in Room 201, phone (417) 256-4001, fax (417) 257-0090. Hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday, including the noon hour, and the office closes on state holidays.

The assessor, Daniel Franks, has Suite 202 at (417) 256-8284 and opens at 8:00 am. His site offers GIS mapping and a subscription parcel search at howell.missouriassessors.com. The collector's duties go beyond houses: it prepares separate statements for personal property such as cars, trucks and boats, for real estate, and for utilities such as railroads and gas lines, and it issues merchant licenses.

How do I pay my Howell County tax bill?

Statements are mailed each November and count as due on receipt. After December 31 they turn delinquent. A mailed check that is postmarked January 1 or later comes back unless it includes late fees. If November ends with no statement in your mailbox, call at once, since the missing paper does not erase the tax.

Ways to pay Howell County property tax, from the Howell County Collector website
MethodDetail
OnlineClick Pay Taxes on the collector's site
Phone1-800-652-0405, current taxes only; enter county number 18 and the PIN from your statement
MailPostmarked no later than December 31
Drop boxOutside the Howell County Office Building
CounterRoom 201, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm

The collector distributes what it collects each month to the taxing entities that levy against your parcel.

Who owes the tax if I sell or move partway through the year?

The assessor's information page quotes RSMo 137.075 and says liability attaches to whoever holds property on January 1, even a buyer who closes that same day. It gives the example of someone leaving Missouri in June 2026: that person is still taxed for 2026 and the law offers no proration.

That page is written around vehicles and other personal property, which taxpayers list with the assessor before March 1. A house is different in practice, since the sale contract and the settlement statement set how the year's real estate bill is divided. Read the proration clause before you sign.

What share of a Howell County home's value is taxed?

Missouri taxes 19 percent of a home's true value, 12 percent of farmland and 32 percent of commercial property, a rule found in RSMo 137.115. Real estate is revalued every odd year.

  • Raises above 15 percent for a home, new building excluded, require an on-site inspection.
  • You may ask for the inspector to come inside, and the notice must give you thirty days to do so.
  • Under RSMo 138.060, the assessor must prove a raise of that size is justified when you appeal.

Pull up your parcel record on the assessor's site before you call, so you can quote the parcel number.

What are my options if the number looks wrong?

The Board of Equalization comes first, with a cutoff on the second Monday in July. The State Tax Commission is next, and it gives you 30 days from the Board's letter. Signing a stipulation with the assessor settles the case for good.

Paying under protest is a separate tool. RSMo 139.031 calls for payment of the whole bill ahead of delinquency, a written explanation filed with the collector, and a lawsuit against the collector within ninety days. The collector holds the contested share in its own fund while the case runs. A tax paid by mistake can be credited or refunded when the taxpayer applies within three years.

When does Howell County auction delinquent property?

The collector's page sets the sale for the fourth Monday in August, and RSMo 140.150 agrees. Until the gavel falls, an owner can settle by paying the tax, penalty, interest and costs. The collector mails notice to the record owner, though a letter that goes astray does not wipe out the debt.

A seller with a balance should ask (417) 256-4001 for a payoff and have the title company wire it from proceeds at closing.

What is the story behind Howell County?

Josiah Howell bought the first settlement in Howell Valley, and the county took his name when it was organized on March 2, 1857. The first circuit court met in a log cabin about a mile east of West Plains, according to an 1876 account. A small wooden courthouse went up on the West Plains square in 1859 and burned in 1862. The county reorganized in 1865, lost its records to a fire in 1866, and built a three-room frame courthouse measuring about 24 by 30 feet in 1869.

Today the county covers 927 square miles of land on the Arkansas line, which makes it the third largest in Missouri by land area. Part of the Mark Twain National Forest lies inside it. West Plains is the seat and largest city, joined by Brandsville, Mountain View and Willow Springs, and the census-designated places of Pomona and South Fork.

Which colleges, libraries and neighboring counties frame a Howell County sale?

Howell County borders Texas, Shannon, Oregon, Ozark and Douglas counties in Missouri and Fulton County in Arkansas. Missouri State University-West Plains, a satellite of Missouri State University, is in the county seat, and the South Central Career Center in West Plains offers vocational and technical programs for grades 9 through 12. Public libraries operate in Mountain View, West Plains and Willow Springs.

Private schools listed for the county include Faith Assembly Christian School and Ozarks Christian Academy in West Plains and Trinity Christian Academy in Mountain View. Population peaked at 40,400 in 2010 and was 39,750 at the 2020 census, with the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate back above 40,000.

What do housing numbers look like in Howell County?

Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 give a picture of a county where most households own:

  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 40,798
  • Housing units: 18,288 across 15,965 households
  • Homes occupied by owners: 70.3%
  • Median owner-occupied value: $173,000
  • Median rent: $733
  • Monthly owner costs: $1,109 with a mortgage and $394 without
  • Persons per household: 2.48, with per capita income of $27,570
  • Median household income: $50,993, with 18.6% of residents in poverty
  • New building permits in 2025: 67

At the 2020 census the median age was 41.5 and 21.0 percent of residents were 65 or older. Roughly 70 percent lived in rural areas. Public schools include West Plains R-7, Willow Springs R-IV and Mountain View-Birch Tree R-III, plus smaller districts such as Fairview, Glenwood, Howell Valley, Junction Hill and Richards. Workers spend about 23 minutes getting to their jobs, and 17.8 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

More questions about Howell County, MO Property Tax Guide

What phone number pays a Howell County tax bill?

Dial 1-800-652-0405 for current taxes. Enter county number 18, then the PIN printed on your statement. Back taxes cannot be paid by that line.

Who is the Howell County assessor?

Daniel Franks, in Suite 202 at 35 Court Square, West Plains. His office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm and answers at (417) 256-8284.

When must personal property be listed in Howell County?

Before March 1 each year, according to the assessor's page. Property is assessed as it stood on January 1.

Is Howell County tax prorated if I leave Missouri?

The assessor says no. The tax rests on what you held on January 1, and the law has no proration. A home sale contract can still split that year's real estate bill between buyer and seller.

Where can I check my Howell County parcel before an appeal?

Use the assessor's site, howell.missouriassessors.com, or call (417) 256-8284. Have your parcel number ready, and file any Board of Equalization appeal by the second Monday in July.

Bills come from a different desk. Questions about a value belong with the assessor. Questions about a balance belong with the collector.

What does Henry County look like on the ground?

Henry County sits in west-central Missouri and touches Johnson, Pettis, Benton, St. Clair, Bates and Cass counties. Its land area is 697 square miles, and another 35 square miles is water. It began in December 1834 as Rives County and took the name Henry in 1841, honoring Patrick Henry. The county site styles it the Model County of the Prairies.

The county's own history page calls agriculture the economic base and says about 80 percent of the county is forested, hilly ground, much of it beside federal land around the 55,600 acre Harry S. Truman Reservoir. Hunters and anglers are a steady presence. State routes 7, 13, 18 and 52 are the main roads, and Jefferson Lines provides intercity bus service.

Clinton, the seat, is the largest town at an estimated 8,945 people. Windsor follows with 2,847, then Urich (492), Calhoun (455), Deepwater (422) and Montrose (375). Blairstown, Brownington and Tightwad have fewer than 100 residents each.

How did Clinton become the seat of Henry County, and what is the courthouse like?

The county site says the first hunters and trappers came through in 1826 and the first settlers arrived in the fall of 1830. In 1836 the site for the seat was chosen and named for DeWitt Clinton, then a New York governor. The first court session met in a home on May 4, 1835.

The first courthouse dates to 1837 and was condemned in 1884, then taken down in 1887. Voters approved a $50,000 bond in 1891, and the contract for the present courthouse went to D. J. Hyde and Company of Sedalia for $47,221 in February 1892. Its cornerstone was laid on June 24, 1892.

What outdoor features affect how Henry County properties are marketed?

The county calls itself a sportsman's paradise. It lists many species of fish in local waters, hunting for deer, coyote, squirrel, turkey and dove, and migratory waterfowl on the Truman Reservoir. A parcel near the shoreline, or one with timber and creek frontage, will be described differently from a town lot in Clinton or Windsor, and the assessor's classification can differ too, since farm and residential ground carry different assessment rates.

Which school districts and libraries serve Henry County homes?

Buyers of a Henry County house usually ask which district it falls in, and the assessor's parcel record answers that. Districts anchored in the county include:

  • Henry County R-1 in Windsor
  • Calhoun R-VIII, Montrose R-XIV, Davis R-XII, Leesville R-IX and Shawnee R-III
  • Lakeland R-III, which serves Deepwater and Lowry City and is physically in St. Clair County

Private options include Holy Rosary Catholic School in Clinton, St. Mary's School in Montrose and the Windsor Amish Schools. The Henry County Library and its Lenora Blackmore Branch serve the public.

How does Missouri set the taxable value of a Henry County house?

The assessor applies a fixed share of market value: 19 percent for homes, 12 percent for farmland, 32 percent for commercial property, according to RSMo 137.115. Fresh values go on the books in odd-numbered years and hold through the even year that follows.

  • A jump of more than 15 percent on a home, apart from new construction, triggers an on-site inspection.
  • The owner is told in writing and has 30 days or more to request a look inside.
  • A drive-by does not satisfy the statute.

If such a jump is appealed, RSMo 138.060 puts the burden on the assessor to show the value is no higher than market value.

How can a Henry County owner challenge a value?

The first stop is the county Board of Equalization, with a filing cutoff the State Tax Commission gives as the second Monday in July. A ruling against you can go to the Commission, which allows 30 days from the date of the Board's letter. Filing is online, by email to Legal@stc.mo.gov or by post to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102-0146.

Property held by a company, trust or estate needs a lawyer to file. Your complaint should carry the tax bill or the Board's letter, and nothing else at first. An agreed value signed with the assessor closes the door on further appeal. Call 660-885-7212 for the local forms.

What dates matter on a Henry County tax calendar?

Missouri taxes whoever holds the property on January 1. A Henry County owner or seller should watch these dates:

  • January 1: assessment date
  • Odd years: new real estate values
  • Second Monday in July: Board of Equalization filing cutoff
  • December 31: bill due, with mailed payments judged by postmark under RSMo 139.100
  • After January 1: penalty added by the collector
  • Fourth Monday in August: sale of delinquent land

Call the collector for this year's mailing date and the penalty figure.

What if my Henry County house has back taxes when I sell?

Missouri lets the county sell delinquent land on the fourth Monday of August, and RSMo 140.150 lets the owner stop the sale by paying tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector first. Notice goes by first class mail to the recorded owner, and a letter that never shows up cancels nothing.

Request a payoff from 660-885-7207 before you list, then hand the figure to your title company. If you dispute the value, RSMo 139.031 allows payment under protest: full payment before delinquency, a written statement to the collector, and a circuit court suit within ninety days.

The Treasurer, acting as Ex Officio Collector of Revenue, at 100 West Franklin in Clinton. The state directory lists 660-885-7207 for that office.

Which percentage applies to a Henry County residence?

Nineteen percent of true value. Farmland is assessed at 12 percent and commercial property at 32 percent, and the local levy then applies to the assessed figure.

Is there a grace period after December 31 in Henry County?

Missouri judges mailed payments by postmark, and the collector adds a penalty once January 1 arrives. Ask the collector's office whether any exception applies to you.

Could Henry County auction my home over unpaid tax?

Yes, the statute allows a sale of delinquent land on the fourth Monday of August. Paying the tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector before then stops the sale.

How do I reach the Henry County assessor?

Phone 660-885-7212 or stop by 100 West Franklin in Clinton. Weekday hours are 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and appointments outside those hours are available.

Johnson County by the numbers

What kind of county is Johnson County, Missouri?

Johnson County lies in western Missouri with Warrensburg as its seat and largest city. It spans roughly 829 square miles of land and borders Lafayette, Pettis, Henry, Cass and Jackson counties. Warrensburg anchors a micropolitan area that belongs to the larger Kansas City combined statistical area (Wikipedia).

Holden and Knob Noster are the other cities. Centerview, Leeton, Chilhowee and Kingsville are villages, and Whiteman Air Force Base sits beside Knob Noster. The University of Central Missouri is in Warrensburg. Seven public districts serve the county: Warrensburg R-VI, Holden R-III, Knob Noster R-VIII, Johnson County R-VII, Leeton R-X, Kingsville R-I and Chilhowee R-IV.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts put the 2025 population at 56,670, up 4.9% from the 2020 base. Owners occupy 63.5% of homes and renters hold the rest. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $235,700 and median gross rent is $932.

Which Johnson County offices handle property tax?

The county splits the work in three, as its Assessor page explains. The Assessor sets value and updates ownership on the roll, the taxing districts set rates, and the Collector prepares bills, takes payment and passes the money to the districts.

  • Assessor: Johnson County South Annex, 1310 S Maguire St, Suite B, Warrensburg, MO 64093. Phone 660-747-9822.
  • Collector: 1310 S Maguire St, Suite A, Warrensburg, MO 64093. Phone 660-747-5531.
  • Closure: county administrative offices are closed Thursday and Friday, November 26 and 27, 2026, for Thanksgiving.

The Assessor is not responsible for rates, collection or the distribution of money to schools and fire districts. A question about why a levy rose belongs with the district that levies it.

How does Johnson County turn market value into a tax bill?

The county publishes the formula. Market value is multiplied by an adjustment factor to get assessed value, then divided by 100 and multiplied by each district's rate, and the results are added up.

Johnson County assessment factors (Collector, Tax Entities and Rates page)
ClassFactor
Residential19%
Commercial32%
Agricultural12%

The county's worked example uses an assessed value of 21,903 and a combined rate of 7.6697 per $100, which gives $1,679.90. Your own rate depends on the school, fire, ambulance and city districts around your parcel.

Real estate is reassessed in odd-numbered years, and 2027 is next. An owner gets a Change in Assessed Value Notice by mail, typically in June, when assessed value rises by $500 or more, and a notice can arrive in an even year too. It carries no tax estimate. Call the Assessor for one.

What can a Johnson County owner do about a value they dispute?

The county lays out three steps. Check the notice for factual errors, then book an informal hearing with the Assessor if you have evidence of a different value or a data mistake, then file a Property Assessment Appeal Form for a Board of Equalization hearing if the informal talk fails. Hearings run by appointment, and the contact details sit on every mailed notice.

The State Tax Commission's guide says the Board of Equalization filing must be made by the second Monday in July, which will be July 12, 2027. Ask the Assessor or County Clerk for the exact form and office, and for any extension the board grants. A Board decision can go on to the Commission within 30 days of the decision letter.

  • You may owe tax while an appeal is open. Unpaid tax after December 31 draws interest and penalties.
  • Signing a value agreement with the Assessor during a Board appeal makes the matter final, and no State Tax Commission appeal follows.
  • An LLC, trust, estate or corporation must use an attorney for a State Tax Commission appeal.

When does Johnson County property tax come due?

Bills are mailed in late October and become delinquent after December 31. The Collector's FAQ says payments must carry a postmark of December 31 or earlier. A payment postmarked after that date is returned unprocessed unless the late fees are included.

You can check what you owe on the county's Search Taxes page by choosing Real Estate and entering a name, physical address or mailing address. The first number shown is the parcel number. Missouri statute 140.100 sets an 18 percent penalty on each year's delinquency for land in the back tax book, so a lapsed bill grows quickly (RSMo 140.100).

Escrowed owners get their updated tax figures through the mortgage company, though the county reminds them that timely payment still rests with the taxpayer.

Is there senior property tax relief in Johnson County?

Yes. On March 17, 2025 the County Commission passed Ordinance 25-01, which created a Senior Real Estate Tax Credit under section 137.1050. Homeowners 62 and older may qualify for a credit on the primary residence, calculated from tax increases after a starting credit year.

  • The 2026 application window ran April 1 to June 30, 2026 and has closed. Ask the Collector when the next one opens.
  • The credit does not apply to agricultural or commercial property, personal property, voter-approved bond levies or the State Blind Pension levy.
  • All taxes on the homestead must be current to qualify.
  • It does not freeze value, and reassessments continue in odd years.

Sellers should note that the credit does not move with the owner. It stays with the applicant, does not pass to a buyer, and a seller who buys elsewhere must file a new application to set a new starting year.

What happens if Johnson County taxes stay unpaid for years?

Real estate with three years of delinquent tax must be offered at the annual tax certificate sale, held on the fourth Monday in August. The 2026 sale was set for August 24 at 10 a.m. at 301 W Market Street in Warrensburg, and that date has passed. Lists run in a local newspaper for three weeks before the sale.

The buyer purchases a tax lien, not ownership. The owner of record, or anyone with a recorded lien or deed of trust on the property, can redeem for one year and afterward until a collector's deed is issued. Redemption costs the bid amount plus 10% annual interest, and 8% on any later years' tax the buyer paid. A buyer who fails to get a collector's deed within 18 months of the sale loses the lien.

Any bid above the opening amount is held as surplus. It goes to the County Treasurer, and an owner or lienholder must file a claim with the county commission within ninety days after redemption ends, or the money goes to the schools.

How do property taxes affect a Johnson County house sale?

A tax bill left unpaid does not by itself end a sale, because the title company can request a payoff and settle it from the proceeds. Ask the Collector at 660-747-5531 for a payoff that includes penalty and interest, and order it before listing if the house is more than one year behind. A house near the three-year line is the situation to resolve first, because it can reach the August sale.

More questions about Johnson County, MO Property Tax Guide

Where do I pay Johnson County real estate tax?

At the Collector's office, 1310 S Maguire St, Suite A in Warrensburg, or through the county's online payment link. The phone number is 660-747-5531. A mailed payment needs a December 31 postmark.

What is the Johnson County residential assessment rate?

Nineteen percent of market value. Commercial property is 32% and agricultural property 12%. Rates per $100 then come from the districts covering your parcel.

When will Johnson County reassess my house again?

In 2027, since Missouri reassesses real estate in odd-numbered years. A notice goes out by mail, typically in June, if the assessed value rises by $500 or more.

Does the Johnson County senior tax credit pass to the buyer?

No. It stays with the applicant. A buyer who is 62 or older would need a new application, and a seller who moves must apply again for the new home.

How long before Johnson County sells a home for unpaid tax?

A parcel with three years of delinquent tax must be offered at the sale on the fourth Monday in August. The owner can redeem during the following year by paying the bid plus 10% annual interest.

Which McDonald County office does what on a tax bill?

Property tax in McDonald County runs through two courthouse offices. The Assessor sets values and takes questions or appeals. The Collector mails the statements, accepts payment and runs the delinquent tax sale.

  • Collector: 408 Harmon Street, Pineville, MO 64856; mail to PO Box 725; phone (417) 223-7408.
  • Assessor: McDonald County Courthouse, 408 Harmon Street, Pineville; mail to PO Box 726; phone (417) 223-4361 for real estate and mapping.

Address changes on a tax bill go through the Assessor, not the Collector. If you are selling and the bill still carries an old mailing address, fix that first.

What is McDonald County like for a seller?

McDonald County fills the far southwestern corner of Missouri. Arkansas lies to the south and Oklahoma to the west, with Newton County above and Barry County beside it. The county covers 539 square miles of land, was organized in 1849 and has its seat at Pineville. The largest city is Noel, with Anderson, Goodman, Jane, Lanagan and Southwest City among the other incorporated communities. Interstate 49 and U.S. 71 carry traffic north and south, and Routes 43, 59, 76 and 90 cover the rest.

Census estimates for July 2025 show 23,992 residents, 3.0 percent above the 2020 base. The county has 9,940 housing units, and roughly two in three households (67.3 percent) live in a home they own. The five-year survey value for those homes is $154,700, median gross rent is $767, and household income runs $52,375. The county issued 18 building permits in 2025.

The McDonald County R-I School District, based in Anderson, serves most of the county, with campuses in Noel, Pineville, Rocky Comfort, Southwest City and Jane. Small areas fall in other districts, so the school district line on your tax bill matters when you compare homes.

How is a McDonald County home valued?

Every taxable parcel and personal property item is valued as of the January 1 assessment date that state statute sets, and the Missouri State Tax Commission oversees each county assessor. Assessed value is a share of market value, and the share depends on the property class.

McDonald County assessment classes with a worked example on $100,000 of market value
Property classAssessment rateAssessed value on $100,000
Residential19%$19,000
Agricultural12%$12,000
Commercial32%$32,000

The levy then comes from each taxing body that covers the parcel: school districts, road districts, cities, fire districts and others such as a junior college. The Assessor's page adds that McDonald County itself receives no property tax levy for operations and relies on sales tax for day to day funding.

Under RSMo 137.115, new assessed values are set on January 1 of each odd-numbered year and carry into the following even year, except new construction. Because 2026 is an even year, the value on your bill this month carries over from the 2025 reassessment, and the next general reassessment date is January 1, 2027. The same section requires a physical inspection before an assessor raises a residential parcel by more than 15 percent, excluding new construction.

What is the payment deadline for McDonald County taxes?

Personal property and real estate statements leave the Collector's office during the opening week of November each year. Each one is payable as soon as it arrives and turns delinquent once December 31 passes. For the 2026 bills, that means the mailing is already out and the deadline is December 31, 2026.

  • All statements can be paid with a single check, and partial payment cannot be accepted.
  • The Collector takes cash, a personal check, a money order or a credit card, whether you pay at the counter, by mail or online.
  • Payments postmarked after December 31 are returned unprocessed unless late fees are included.
  • If no statement arrives by the end of November, call the Collector. A missing bill does not cancel the debt or any penalty and interest.

Missouri law has the collector add a penalty once taxes go unpaid past the delinquency date (RSMo 139.100). Ask the Collector at (417) 223-7408 for the current penalty and interest percentages before you pay late. The same statute treats a mailed payment as paid on its postmark date.

The Collector also holds the delinquent tax sale in August each year, so a parcel with old unpaid bills can move toward auction long before a seller notices.

What is the route to contest a McDonald County value?

Begin with a call to the Assessor at (417) 223-4361 to request an informal hearing on the value, and bring sales of similar nearby homes, repair estimates or photos that support a lower number. Ask the same office for the filing date for the local equalization board.

If the board leaves the value unchanged, RSMo 138.430 lets an owner appeal to the State Tax Commission by the statutory deadline or 30 days after the board acts finally, whichever falls later. When an appeal is filed, the disputed taxes are impounded in a separate fund instead of going to the taxing bodies.

Missouri also lets a taxpayer pay under protest. Under RSMo 139.031, you settle the whole bill ahead of delinquency and hand the collector a written statement of your grounds. A protest that is not followed by a circuit court suit against the collector within ninety days becomes void. An appeal already pending before the State Tax Commission replaces that suit requirement.

What relief programs apply to McDonald County owners?

The Missouri Department of Revenue runs the Property Tax Credit Claim, often called the circuit breaker. It gives certain senior citizens and 100 percent disabled individuals a credit for part of the property tax or rent they paid, up to $1,100 for owners who own and occupy their home and $750 for renters. The amount depends on taxes paid and total household income, taxable and nontaxable. Questions go to PropertyTaxCredit@dor.mo.gov.

The State Tax Commission also explains a homestead exemption for a former prisoner of war who has a total service-connected disability. The owner must occupy the homestead as a primary residence and give the assessor proof, including a letter from the Department of Veterans Affairs and discharge records or a records center letter showing former prisoner of war status.

Military personnel stationed in the county under orders with a home of record outside Missouri generally do not owe Missouri personal property tax on non-business items, according to the same State Tax Commission FAQ.

What should a McDonald County seller do about unpaid tax?

Treat the tax bill as a closing item. Before listing a McDonald County house, call the Collector for the status of every year on the parcel, then have the closing agent divide the current year's bill between the parties. A parcel with delinquent years can reach the August sale, so clear older balances first.

  • Check the owner name and mailing address on file at the Assessor's office.
  • Request a payoff figure from the Collector for every parcel you are selling, including land and any manufactured home.
  • Keep your settlement statement, because it shows how the year's tax was split.
  • If the assessed value looks high, raise it with the Assessor before the board deadline rather than after closing.

More questions about McDonald County, MO Property Tax Guide

What date makes a McDonald County tax bill late?

Anything unpaid after December 31. Bills go out the first week of November, and a payment postmarked in January comes back unless late fees ride along.

Can I pay half of my McDonald County bill now and half later?

No. The Collector states that partial payment cannot be accepted, though all statements can be paid together with one check.

What assessment rate applies to a McDonald County house?

Houses carry a 19 percent rate, farmland 12 percent and commercial parcels 32 percent of market value. A $100,000 home therefore shows $19,000 of assessed value before any levy is applied.

Where do I send an address correction for my tax statement?

The Assessor's office at (417) 223-4361. The Collector's site routes address changes there.

When is the McDonald County delinquent tax sale?

The Collector holds the delinquent tax sale in August. Call the Collector at (417) 223-7408 for the exact date and the parcels listed.

Which offices handle property tax in Dunklin County, Missouri?

Two elected offices in the Kennett courthouse split the work. The assessor decides what a parcel is worth, and the collector mails the bill and takes the money. Both are at 100 Kennett Court Square, Kennett, MO 63857, and both keep weekday hours listed in the table further down.

The collector page lists Judy Thompson as Collector-Treasurer, with Room 203, a mailing address of PO Box 445 and phone 573-888-2180. The assessor is Rena Ingram, at 573-888-1409 or 573-888-4771. Angela Casey is the recorder of deeds, in Room 204, at 573-888-3468.

The collector sends out money for every body that levies tax on Dunklin County property:

  • The ambulance district and the health center
  • The library and the schools
  • The state and the townships
  • The road and bridge fund and the sheltered workshop

City taxes are a separate bill. The collector says they go to the city, and a county check should never be mailed together with a city payment.

What does a seller need to know about Dunklin County itself?

Dunklin County sits in the Bootheel, the far southeastern corner of Missouri, and Kennett is the seat of government and the biggest town. The county was cut from Stoddard County in 1845 and named for Governor Daniel Dunklin. The state's lowest point is here, where the St. Francis River leaves Missouri for Arkansas in Buffalo Township, and the county lies south of 36 degrees 30 minutes north, which puts most of it in the Sun Belt by one research definition.

Besides Kennett, the incorporated places are Arbyrd, Campbell, Cardwell, Clarkton, Holcomb, Hornersville, Malden and Senath, plus the town of Rives. Census-designated places include Frisbee, Hollywood and White Oak. Buyers in a Dunklin County town pay both a county and a city tax bill, so ask each office what is owed.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts for Dunklin County give a feel for the housing market:

  • 26,855 residents in the July 2025 estimate, down 5.1 percent from the April 2020 base of 28,292
  • 13,520 housing units, with 62.3 percent of homes occupied by their owners
  • $97,600 median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024
  • $648 median gross rent and $47,849 median household income
  • Only 30 permits for new building in 2025

A median home value under $100,000 means a tax bill is often a few hundred dollars, so a small delinquency can still be a large share of a seller's equity. Pull the statement early.

How does the Dunklin County assessor set the value of a house?

Missouri law has the assessor list all taxable real property each year, with new values set as of January 1 of each odd-numbered year. Those values carry into the even-numbered year, except for new construction. Under RSMo 137.115, a home is assessed at 19 percent of true value, farmland at 12 percent and commercial property at 32 percent, so a $100,000 house carries $19,000 of assessed value before the levy is applied.

If the assessor wants to raise a residential parcel by more than 15 percent, apart from new building, a physical inspection has to happen first. The owner can ask for an interior look and has at least 30 days to make that request. A drive-by does not count.

An owner who changes how a property is used, for example from farm to residential, may apply to the assessor for reclassification. The assessor's page for Dunklin County says the office aims for equitable and accurate appraisals, and it also hosts a personal property filing link online.

How do I appeal a Dunklin County assessment?

Start with the notice. When an assessor raises a value, RSMo 137.180 requires word to the record owner, mailed to the last known address, and in a reassessment year the notice is due by June 15. Call the assessor's office at the numbers above if the new value looks off, and bring sale prices of similar houses.

The formal route is the county Board of Equalization, which hears appeals from the assessor's value under RSMo 138.060 and starts with no presumption that the assessor is right. In a county outside the charter group, the assessor carries the burden of proof only where the value rose 15 percent or more and the cause was not new building. The State Tax Commission says a Board appeal must be filed by the second Monday in July. For 2027 that falls on July 12. Ask the Dunklin County Clerk where the form goes.

If the Board's decision stands, the next step is the State Tax Commission, which takes a complaint by September 30 or within 30 days after the Board's final action, whichever is later. Appeals for property owned by an LLC, corporation, trust, estate or limited partnership must be filed by an attorney. Attach the tax bill or the Board decision letter, and hold other evidence until the Commission asks for it.

When are Dunklin County property taxes due, and what does a late bill cost?

The State Tax Commission puts the due date at December 31 each year. Mailed payments count as paid on the postmark date under RSMo 139.100, so a December 31 postmark is on time. After January 1 the collector adds a penalty, and RSMo 140.100 sets it at 18 percent of each year's delinquency, with a cap of 2 percent per month on land redeemed before the sale.

The Dunklin County collector has house rules worth knowing before anyone drives to Kennett:

  • Send the statement back with the payment, or the check is returned and an in-person payer pays to print a duplicate
  • Partial payments and part-cash, part-check payments are refused
  • Cash, credit and debit cards, personal checks with an address, phone and driver license number, bank checks and money orders are accepted
  • Older delinquent taxes must be paid before current taxes are taken
  • No tax information is given by phone. Visit Room 203, fax the office (a $3 fee applies per parcel) or write

A homeowner disputing the value can still pay under protest. Pay the full bill before the delinquency date, write a statement of the reasons with the claimed value, and file suit against the collector within 90 days under RSMo 139.031. A refund claim for tax paid by mistake must be filed within three years.

What happens at the Dunklin County delinquent tax sale?

The collector runs the sale on the fourth Monday of August, which is the date written into RSMo 140.150. The collector's page says real estate with taxes two years old is offered each August. The 2026 sale has passed, and the collector posted a notice in October 2026 about properties left after a third offering, with deeds issued immediately on purchase.

The statute lets the owner pay taxes, penalty, interest and costs at any time before the sale. Notice goes first by regular mail to the owner of record. A certified second notice follows when the assessed value is over $1,000. Not receiving the notice does not erase the tax.

An owner of a Dunklin County house with old tax years should treat the August calendar as a hard stop. Settling the balance before that Monday keeps the house out of the offering, and after the sale the owner's choices narrow.

All three offices share one courthouse square. The table below pulls the details from each county page.

What should I do about taxes when selling a Dunklin County house?

Ask the collector for a current statement, and pay any old year first, since current taxes are not accepted ahead of delinquent ones. Give the title company the parcel number and the collector's phone, so the payoff matches the office's records. The sales contract sets how the current year's bill is divided between buyer and seller, so have the title company read that clause.

The recorder's fee schedule changed on August 27, 2026. A one-page document now costs $26, and each added page up to 20 pages costs $3 more, so a three-page deed is $32. Plats and surveys have their own rates. The recorder says Missouri counties accept electronic filing through a shared portal, so ask the office if a title company will file that way.

When liens, tenants or repairs pile up on a Kennett-area house, a written cash offer is one way out, and the tax payoff is taken from the price at closing.

The Dunklin County Collector-Treasurer, Judy Thompson, sends it from Room 203 of the Kennett courthouse. The assessor, Rena Ingram, only sets the value. City taxes are paid to the city, so check that bill separately.

What is the Dunklin County property tax deadline?

December 31. The State Tax Commission gives that date, and a mailed payment is on time if postmarked by then. Penalty starts the next day under RSMo 140.100 at 18 percent of the year's delinquency.

Can I pay part of my Dunklin County bill?

No. The collector accepts only the full amount due and does not take partial or part-cash, part-check payments. Pay the oldest delinquent year first, because current taxes are not taken until delinquent ones are cleared.

When does Dunklin County sell tax-delinquent houses?

On the fourth Monday of August each year, under RSMo 140.150. The collector offers real estate with taxes two years old. You can pay the taxes, penalty and costs any time before the sale.

How do I contest my Dunklin County home value?

Call the assessor first, then file with the Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. If the Board does not change the value, file with the State Tax Commission by September 30 or a month after the Board decision, whichever is later.
